brief: Goldman's mid-day US equities color (Nov 13) frames today's index weakness as concentrated in AI/semiconductors rather than broad-based: 60% of S&P 500 constituents are higher and the index excluding AI (SPXXAI) is up 40bps even as headline indices trade red. NVDA is down 3.3% (erasing roughly $500bn of market cap week-to-date), AVGO -5.2% and AMD -10.6%, dragging the broader GSTMTSEM semiconductor index down 3.8%. Unlike yesterday's intra-sector rotation, where some semis outperformed, today's selloff is sector-wide, and hyperscalers are the beneficiaries of the rotation out of semis. Separately, the note's chart highlights hyperscaler valuations: their P/E has fallen sharply and nearly closed the gap with the rest of the index, making them look attractive. This morning's PPI print pushed rates higher and led Goldman's economics team to lower its core PCE estimate, while crude trades above $95, adding to the day's pressure. Flows are skewed 14.5% better for sale across the franchise, with both hedge funds and long-only accounts net selling, concentrated in tech, macro products and consumer services. Next week: Warsh speaks Monday, NVDA reports earnings Tuesday.
